items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: I said Everett Thomas C., I said, well, I worked for him when I was a kid.

ctx.x: Oh, no, no, no. The only thing it had was this big dance. It was an open dance hall. The sides were open and it had a roof on it and had... It was about six feet off of the ground, huh? Five feet off of the ground. Oh, was it? Four feet off of the ground, something like that. I don't remember that.

I know when I opened up the place, the platform was on the ground and we had a canvas tarpaulin over the dance floor then, Emmett and Joe Lloyd Cannon, and Chink. Well, we sat outside the dance floor and had regular shavings, wood shavings out there, you know? And we sat there then. Yeah. The first night we opened the midway. But then they put a roof over there and had a real nice dance floor, a bandstand, you know? I think it was the guy's name that ran the place. His name was Everett Thomas C., wasn't he?
I was about to ask you. That name is familiar, Thomas C., I must have heard it somewhere. Everett Thomas C., yeah.
